newsitem.title: CHINA: Moody's deals blow to top-rated Korean banks.
newsitem.headline: Moody's deals blow to top-rated Korean banks.

text.p: Korean offshore bonds were dealt another blow on Thursday after Moody's Investors Service said four top-rated banks had a negative outlook.
"Korean paper is dead quiet, and I don't know when it will pick up anymore," a trader at a U.S. commercial bank said.

The four banks, Housing and Commercial Bank of Korea, Industrial Bank of Korea, Korea Development Bank and Export-Import Bank of Korea, all have senior long-term debt ratings of A1, equal to the sovereign's credit ceiling.
The rating outlook reflects the negative outlook for Korea's sovereign rating ceiling, Moody's said.
Spreads have been widening for all Korean banks amid massive defaults among Korean conglomerates, but the impact has been comparatively smaller for the sovereign-related credits.
However, the Moody's move on Thursday changed the situation.
"I would expect spreads to widen by a couple of basis points for sovereign-related credits," a Japanese bank trader said.

Korea Development Bank's outstanding fixed-rate yankee bond due 2006 widened to 100 basis points over comparable U.S. Treasuries during Asian trading hours from 87/86 basis points before the Moody's news.
The bond is currently consolidating at 92 basis points, traders said.
Industrial Bank of Korea's US$50 million floating rate note issue scheduled for general syndication this week has been postponed.
Sources close to the transaction said the delay was due "purely to administrative matters" but other bankers blamed the Moody's action for the decision.
IBK's FRN has a final maturity of three years with annual put and call options.
The issue was expected to be priced at par to float at 25 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate. Fees were two basis points giving an all-in return of 27 basis points, bankers noted.
Sanwa International Finance was the mandated arranger.
Moody's announcement came one day after an announcement by Standard and Poor's Corp on Wednesday that it might cut the ratings of five South Korean banks, all of which are rated below the sovereign.
The five banks were Korea First Bank, Hanil Bank, Korea Long Term Credit Bank. Shinhan Bank and Korea Exchange Bank.
